I woke up late one morning, which honestly happens more than I'd like to admit these days, and I basically threw on the first shirt I grabbed from my closet.
No mirror, no real thought, just straight out the door as fast as I could go.
I rushed through my morning like normal, grabbed coffee, caught the bus, and made it to work only a few minutes late, which felt like a small personal victory considering how late I'd woken up.
I sat down at my desk, said good morning to a few coworkers, and got straight into my emails.
About an hour later, my coworker Dana walked by, glanced at me, and just kind of paused mid-step.
She had this look on her face like she wanted to say something but wasn't totally sure if she should.
I asked what was wrong, and she quietly pointed at my shirt.
I looked down, and there they were, the seams, the little tag sticking out near my collar, the whole thing completely inside out.
I had been walking around the office for a full hour like that, saying good morning to people, completely unaware the entire time.
Honestly, my first instinct was to just pretend I hadn't noticed and keep going, like maybe nobody else would say anything about it.
But then I remembered I'd already walked past at least five people, including my manager, during a hallway conversation about a project deadline earlier that morning.
I ducked into the bathroom, fixed the shirt as quickly as I possibly could, and came back out acting like nothing had happened at all.

Dana, of course, told at least two other people before I even sat back down, so by lunchtime, pretty much everyone had heard about it, including people from a completely different floor who had no real reason to know.
A guy from IT I'd never even spoken to stopped by my desk just to ask if I was doing okay, which honestly made the whole thing feel even bigger than it actually was.

My manager actually brought it up during our meeting, completely straight-faced, and said something like, "Nice look this morning, very avant-garde." I wasn't even sure what that meant, but I laughed anyway because at that point, there wasn't much else left to do.
Now I always check my shirt before leaving the house, every single time, no matter how late I'm running that day, even glancing in the hallway mirror just to be sure.
My roommate still brings up the inside-out shirt whenever I complain about being tired in the morning, like it's some kind of permanent warning label on my mornings.
